intro: Training starts with a prediction and a direction for improvement. For linear regression, those directions can be computed exactly.
task: Return a dictionary with `loss`, `dw`, and `db` for predictions `X @ w + b` and loss `mean((prediction - y)**2) / 2`.
requirements: X has shape (n, d), y has shape (n,), w has shape (d,), and b is a finite scalar.
Require n >= 1 and d >= 1. Reject non-finite values and incompatible shapes with ValueError.
Return dw as a NumPy array and loss/db as numeric scalars. Average gradients over the batch.
Do not modify any input. Evaluation uses moderate finite values.

hints.title: Keep the residual
hints.body: Let residual = X @ w + b - y. Its sign determines which direction reduces the prediction error.

hints.title: Differentiate each parameter
hints.body: For a weight, multiply the residual by that feature. For the bias, its derivative in every prediction is one.

hints.title: Match the loss scaling
hints.body: The factor 1/2 cancels the derivative of the square. Divide both gradients by n, not by the number of features.

explanation: Each residual contributes to the gradient. Matrix multiplication X.T @ residual adds all feature-weighted residuals in one operation.
Because the loss averages over examples, its gradient must average too. Using a sum instead changes the effective step size whenever the batch size changes.
The derivative of a prediction with respect to b is one, so db is simply the mean residual. These gradients can be checked independently by finite differences.
